title: Panelist rotation and core competency mapping playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a repeatable protocol to rotate interview panelists across hiring programs and to map each role’s core competencies to standardized question banks and scoring anchors. Designed for People Ops partnering with hiring managers, interviewers, and hiring committees. Focus: reduce bias, spread institutional knowledge, shorten ramp time for new panelists, and provide clear audit trails during selection.

Context and goals (short):
- We have many overlapping interview loops across eng, product, and infra teams; panels concentrate experience in a few people and create scheduling bottlenecks.
- Goal: create a 12-week rotation cycle so panel experience is distributed, ensure each panelist covers at least 3 competency areas, and enable rapid calibration every 6 weeks.
- Outcome metrics: panel fill rate >= 95%, time-to-offer reduced by 10%, inter-panel score variance < 12% on same role over a quarter.

Audience:
- People Ops (owners of rotation cadence)
- Hiring managers (role competency owners)
- Interviewers/panelists (contributors)
- Recruiting coordinators (scheduling & logistics)

Key definitions (single-line):
- Panelist: Redwood employee who conducts interviews.
- Competency: A cluster of skills/behaviors we expect for a role (e.g., System Design, Inference Runtime, Debugging, Communication).
- Rotation cohort: group of panelists assigned to cover interviews for a set of roles for a cycle.

High-level protocol:
1) Role competency mapping (week 0–1)
   - Hiring manager completes the Competency Canvas for the open role (link to template). Canvas lists top 4 competencies and desired evidence.
   - People Ops maps each competency to 2–3 canonical probes from the standardized bank and selects scoring anchors (0–3).

2) Panel assembly and target distribution (week 1–2)
   - People Ops proposes a 6-person panel pool per hiring program. Aim: 40% cross-functional, 60% role-aligned.
   - Each panelist is assigned 1 primary competency and 1 backup. No one will be primary for more than 2 roles per cycle.

3) Onboarding new panelists (week 2)
   - Quick-start checklist for new panelists:
     * Read role Competency Canvas and rubric (15 min).
     * Watch two 8-minute calibration videos (role-specific) and take the 10-question quiz.
     * Join 1 shadow interview with an experienced panelist (observe, 30–60 min).
     * Complete short commitment form (availability blocks, conflict-of-interest check).
   - Coordinator adds them to the panel rotation calendar and Slack channel.

4) Running interviews and scoring (ongoing)
   - Use the shared rubric sheet during interview; score each competency 0–3 with a one-sentence evidence note.
   - Recruiter collects scores and uploads them to the candidate folder within 24 hours.

5) Weekly spot checks and logs (ongoing)
   - People Ops runs a weekly report: panel attendance, missing feedback, average time to submit feedback.
   - Any missing feedback >48h triggers an auto-reminder and flags the hiring manager.

6) Bi-weekly calibration (every 6 weeks recommended)
   - 60-minute session: 3 recorded anonymized interview excerpts are reviewed; panelists re-score with anchors visible.
   - Outcome: adjust anchors, update question phrasing, and note any panelist outlier behavior for coaching.

7) Rotation handoff and retrospective (end of cycle)
   - Handover doc created with: what worked, scheduling pain points, score variance, and recommended follow-ups.
   - People Ops updates the competency bank if new evidence types emerged.

Competency mapping template (summary):
- Competency name (single line)
- Behavioral anchors (3 bullet lines)
- Canonical probes (2–3 short interview prompts)
- High/Medium/Low evidence examples (single-sentence each)
- Typical role weight (0–100)

Scoring anchors (0–3):
- 0: No evidence or harmful behavior.
- 1: Limited or inconsistent evidence; major gaps remain.
- 2: Solid, meets expectations with minor gaps.
- 3: Strong evidence; would recommend.

Sample competency: Runtime debugging (example):
- Behavioral anchors: isolates root cause, uses telemetry, communicates tradeoffs.
- Canonical probes: "Describe a time you traced a production memory leak in a model-serving process."; "Walk me through how you’d triage slow token generation during peak load."
- Evidence examples: High: produced clear RCA and mitigations; Medium: identified probable cause but lacked mitigation plan; Low: unable to localize issues.
- Typical role weight: 70

Interviewer onboarding checklist (practical):
- Sign conflict-of-interest disclosure (yes/no)
- Confirm availability windows in scheduling tool
- Complete shadow interview and quiz
- Review last two retros for the hiring program
- Add your standard question set to the shared bank (if new)

Calibration exercise (script for facilitator):
- 0–5m: intro, objectives, anonymization reminder.
- 5–20m: play clip 1, individual scoring with anchors.
- 20–35m: discuss discrepancies; ask panelists to defend evidence notes.
- 35–50m: update anchor wording and log the change.
- 50–60m: action items, who will coach which panelists, update training materials.

Hard edge rules (for fairness & speed):
- No candidate may be interviewed by the same person more than once across the primary loop unless agreed by hiring manager.
- All feedback must be submitted within 24 hours; exceptions only by prior agreement.
- If a panelist misses 3 scheduled interviews in a cycle without notice, they are removed from that cycle and receive a coaching follow-up.

Data & reporting (minimum fields):
- Candidate id, role, interview date, panelist, competency scores (0–3), evidence note, time to feedback (hours), interview recording id.
- People Ops will maintain a quarterly dashboard with score distributions and panelist workload.

Playbook maintenance & ownership:
- People Ops: owner for rotation cadence, reporting, onboarding flow, and logistics.
- Hiring manager: owner for competency canvas accuracy and final question selection.
- People Ops + Hiring managers: joint owners of the canonical question bank.

Quick templates & links (placeholders):
- Competency Canvas template: CONFLUENCE-CC-2025
- Onboarding quiz: https://forms.redwood.ai/panel-onboard-quiz
- Recording retention policy: HR-REC-2024
- Scheduling: calendar/panel-rotation-2025

Open questions & follow-ups (for next planning sync):
- Should we centralize all canonical probes in a Redwood Git repo to make PR-driven edits and history easier?
- How many cross-functional slots are ideal for small hiring programs (<6 hires/mo)? Pilot 1:1 ratio for two quarters.
- Define Light-touch vs Heavy-touch roles and map required calibration cadence.

Notes to reviewers (Asha):
- This is intentionally process-first; we will package sample training videos and two anonymized clips for the first calibration.
- Recommend running a pilot for two hiring programs (serving-runtime interns and product infra ICs) in Q4 2025.

Revision history (top-line):
